messages.subject: expected behavior for `profile`
messages.body_plain:
I'm relatively new to using the `profile` argument in TMB and RTMB.  I had assumed that it would speed up convergence in cases where fixed effects are highly correlated with random effects (which causes the inner and outer optimizers to slowly move along the resulting ridge), but would not affect the resulting MLE or objective value for the MLE (because it is not including the profile`ed fixed effects in the Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood).  I observe this expected behavior in simple models (3 slopes being profiled), e.g., using tinyVAST.

However, I have a very large model (80 slopes being profiled and another 12 loadings not being profiled in a spatial-factor model) where profiling the slopes results in a ~0.005 difference in MLE relative to not profiling the slopes, even though it's using 2 newtonsteps and each run has a max-absolute-gradient of <10^-9 with respect to remaining fixed effects.

Questions:
Is it true that profiling should not affect the MLE or objective value for the MLE?
Any intuition about cases when machine-precision round errors might cause this not to be true?
Jim

messages.subject: RTMB advector issue when assigning to Matrix object
messages.subject_clean: RTMB advector issue when assigning to Matrix object
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I'm trying to implement a geostatistical model using RTMB, so in other words, I'm rewriting sdmTMB models in RTMB. I'm encountering an issue when incorporating anisotropy: creating the precision matrix Q needed for anisotropy causes issues with advectors, in that there are no methods yet for assigning a RHS advector value into a LHS sparse matrix via indexing:

> mat <- Matrix::Matrix(0, nrow = 2 , ncol = 2) > mat[1,1] <- advector(2) Error in .local(x, i, j, ..., value) : not-yet-implemented 'Matrix[<-' method

To highlight this issue in relation to geostatistical precision matrices, I've written a short-ish MWE that helps with understanding the barrier with implementing anisotropy in RTMB:

https://gist.github.com/sebpardo/9a7c63f2a9fd57b5e664c07dd14e7ec8

It seems to me there are a few  ways of potentially resolving this issue:

1. Implement 'Matrix[<-' method for advectors.
2. Compile R_inla.hpp as R objects and use those Q SPDE functions instead of R ones.
3. Move away from using sparse matrices for the precision matrix to a simpler "base" matrix (`advector`). I explored using this but encountered other errors along the way, and I'm not sure if it would be a fruitful avenue.
4. Calling `RTMB::getValues` within `Q_spde_aniso()` to remove RHS advector and avoid matrix assignment issue, for example replacing line 72 of the MWE with:

G1_aniso[TV[i, 2] , TV[i, 1] ] <- G1_aniso[TV[i, 2] , TV[i, 1] ] + RTMB:::getValues(Gtmp[i, 1, 2])
and so on until line 80. However, this is likely to mess up with the tape and is probably not advisable, and also throws an error ("Not compatible with requested type: [type=language; target=double]") when `Q_spde_aniso()`returns the final object.

I'm unsure how to proceed from here, so any thoughts and suggestions are most welcome!

Thanks,

Seb

messages.subject: Re: RTMB advector issue when assigning to Matrix object
messages.subject_clean: RTMB advector issue when assigning to Matrix object
messages.body_plain:
The recently added RTMB::AD constructor can sort out such overload issues - example very close to what you want is on the help page ?AD.
In general, if you need to sub-assign to non-AD object from AD object, it's probably best to use e.g. :

G1_aniso <- AD(Matrix::Matrix(0, nrow = n_s, ncol = n_s))
Gtmp <- AD(array(0, dim = c(n_tri, 3, 3)))

In non-AD contexts the AD(.) is ignored, while in AD contexts an appropriate conversion takes place.

messages.subject: Quadratic form for GMRF precision
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

TMB and RTMB include helpful functions to calculate the density function for a GMRF given a sparse precision Q.  However, in many cases (e.g., the SPDE method or nearest neighbor GP) the precision Q results from a quadratic form Q = (I-G^T) D (I-G) where I is an identity matrix, D is a diagonal matrix, and G is a sparse path matrix.

Has anyone compared the efficiency of the built-in GMRF density functions against alternative calculations that use the quadratic form, i.e., calculating the det(Q) vs. det(I-G)^2 \times det(D)?

Cheers,
Jim
